recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not reinstate the FHIR-6339 DSTU warning; future changes to pattern-based discrimination should be handled through a new FHIR-I decision.
issue_request: FHIR-6339 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core issue asking whether slicing discriminators were compatible with ElementDefinition pattern[x] constraints; its resolution was to temporarily note during DSTU that pattern[x] was not recommended for discrimination until the issue was investigated.
initial_application: Historical git-svn commit 63a62f03c95b6d77d7d13eb0b5794d6c5c4a2103, svn revision 5863, applied the issue by adding a source/profiling.html note that fixed values or required value set bindings should be used for slicing and pattern[x] was not recommended while the issue was investigated. Later discriminator rework in 3253654af7787e9b738b15f4618a2b9d02d56f7f removed that temporary caution.
additional_context: FHIR-13672 explicitly allowed pattern[x] in discriminator ElementDefinitions, and FHIR-25206 later merged value and pattern discriminator behavior by deprecating the pattern discriminator type while documenting that value discrimination can use fixed values, pattern values, or required value set bindings. FHIR-I minutes and linked Zulip discussions for FHIR-25206 confirm the work group considered the pattern/fixed/value-set distinction and chose that merged rule. FHIR-34152 subsequently improved fixed[x] and pattern[x] explanation and links without changing the discriminator conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current build-scoped source already says value discrimination can use fixed, pattern, or required binding constraints and that the pattern discriminator type has the same meaning as value for backwards compatibility, so no source edit is needed.
